subject: Hosted API spend safeguards & emergency handling
messages:
From: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@heliomed.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@heliomed.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on spend caps / emergency cutoffs

Hi Neha,

Quick one as we finalize the procurement note for our security/compliance team: what exactly happens if our hosted API usage goes beyond the monthly budget cap? Our procurement lead is asking whether Redwood will: 1) immediately cut requests once a hard cap is reached, 2) throttle to slower rates, or 3) bill overage at the standard rate (and how quickly we’d be notified).

We need this spelled out in the SOW (and any auto-cutoff specifics for sensitive workloads). Can you send the precise behaviors and any recommended guardrails?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Bennett
Head of Platform Ops, HelioMed
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@heliomed.com>, procurement@heliomed.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick question on spend caps / emergency cutoffs

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. Below is how Redwood handles spend caps for Hosted API (short version first, then details you can drop into the SOW):

Short summary (pick one of these operational models):
- Hard cut (customer-configurable): once the monthly spend cap is hit, new requests return 429 with a specific error code X-Spend-Limit. No tokens are billed beyond the cap. Useful for strict budget enforcement.
- Soft cap + throttle: traffic continues but is throttled to a defined rps/token rate (you set the throttle profile). Overage is billed at the regular per-token rate; we send alerts and apply per-request latency/backoff.
- Alert-only (monitoring): no automatic action — we send multi-channel alerts at thresholds (70/85/100%) and leave control to your infra/automation. Overage billed normally.

Details for inclusion in SOW:
- Notification cadence: email + webhook at 70%, 90%, and immediate on cap breach. HelioMed can specify a single webhook endpoint for automated mitigation.
- Emergency cutoff window: if "hard cut" is selected, cutoff is immediate; we provide a console toggle to lift the cap with IAM controls and audit logs.
- Billing behavior: for soft-cap and alert-only, usage beyond the cap is invoiced on the next billing cycle at the agreed per-token rate. Pro-rated credits are available for documented service disruptions (covered under SLA).
- Retry semantics: 429 errors include Retry-After and X-Spend-Limit headers to help clients implement backoff and graceful degradation.
- Escalation: for sustained overages >48 hours we route to a named account lead (Marissa) and can open a temporary committed burst window subject to approval.

Recommended guardrail we’ve seen work well: hard cap in production for expensive downstream workflows + a soft-cap/test environment with throttling to allow internal experiments.

I’ve attached a short PDF with the templated SOW paragraph and the SOW draft for your legal team to review.

Want me to loop in Marissa to propose commercial options (temporary burst, overage discounts, or a mid-month true-up)?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Regional Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: heliomed_spend_policy.pdf, SOW_HelioMed_v2.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Quick question on spend caps / emergency cutoffs

Tom — copying Marissa (sales) wrote? Oops, that's me. Quick commercial note: if HelioMed expects bursty research workloads, we can offer two practical concessions: 1) a one-time safety buffer (10-15% above your committed monthly cap) that is billed at a discounted overage rate (we typically apply a 20% discount on overage for the buffer), or 2) a short-term committed uplift (30-day commit) which reduces the unit cost and removes hard cut risk.

Both options require sign-off but can be added to an addendum that references the SOW paragraph Neha drafted. If you want, I’ll prepare a short amendment with pricing and an explicit rollback trigger.

—Marissa

Thanks — that helps. A couple follow-ups: 1) for audit purposes we need the exact header name and value Redwood will include on 429s so our middleware can detect it. 2) if we go with the hard cut option, can we get a one-click emergency bypass in the console that requires MFA + logs the operator? Procurement is adamant about human approval flows.

We’re also evaluating whether to set the cap at a dollar amount or token budget; which do you recommend?

Tom
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@heliomed.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick question on spend caps / emergency cutoffs

Tom — quick answers inline: 
- Header names: when a hard cut triggers we return HTTP 429 with headers: X-Spend-Limit: hard, X-Spend-Usage: {current_usd_cents}, and Retry-After set in seconds. For soft cap throttle you will receive X-Spend-Limit: soft and X-Throttle-Rate (rps) in the response.
- Console bypass: yes — we have an "Emergency Cap Lift" workflow that requires MFA and logs the operator (we capture user id, timestamp, and reason). We can include that flow in the SOW as a required control.
- Dollar vs token cap: dollar caps are simpler for procurement/accounting; token caps are more precise for engineering. Recommendation: set a primary dollar cap for billing governance + a secondary token threshold alert to catch model shifts (e.g., long-generation bursts).

If you'd like, I can produce a one-page technical appendix with header examples, sample webhook payloads, and a recommended middleware pattern for graceful degradation.

—Rishi (Platform Reliability)
